title: Keel's Ethereum emergency protocol is a pre-written three-step unwind: redeem every position, consolidate into USDS, burn the debt
content:
A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.2.2.1.3 does not describe emergency principles; it gives the calls. Redeem all ERC-4626 positions with `redeemERC4626(address(token), token.balanceOf(address(proxy)))` (…3.2.1), consolidate with `swapUSDCToUSDS(usdc.balanceOf(address(proxy))` (…3.3), and repay with `burnUSDS(usds.balanceOf(address(proxy))` (…3.4). Alongside sits the Freezer's own tool, `removeRelayer(address relayer)` (…3.1).

The notable feature is that every argument is a balance lookup. An operator executing the playbook makes no sizing decisions, chooses no venues, and needs no view about market conditions — the sequence is mechanical and reproducible under stress by whoever holds the keys, which is exactly what an emergency procedure must be.

The order encodes the goal: positions first (out of third-party protocols), then currency consolidation (out of USDC into USDS), then debt extinction (`wipe` against the Allocation Vault). The end state is that Keel owes Sky nothing and holds nothing anywhere else — the maximally de-risked configuration, reached by moving exposure inward one layer at a time.

This is also the clause that justifies the asymmetric rate limits elsewhere in the Artifact. Every step of the playbook is an unwinding operation, and every unwinding operation is Unlimited; had withdrawal or burn been capped, the documented emergency procedure would be unexecutable in a large emergency, which is the only kind that matters.
description: The playbook calls redeemERC4626 with the full share balance, swapUSDCToUSDS with the full USDC balance, then burnUSDS with the full USDS balance — each parameterized by balance, not by judgment.
